```{r}

library(dplyr)

# read data
data <- read.csv(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/sara_data_VM.csv",
  na.strings = "-999"
)

```

```{r}
names(data)
```


```{r}
attention <- c(
  "meanrt",
  "stdrt",
  "err_com",
  "err_om",
  "imp_err3",
  "imp_err_total",
  "d_prime",
  "dsm_inatten",
  "bis_first",
  "bis_second"
)

resilience <- c(
  "cdrisc",
  "cyrm_total",
  "cyrm_personal",
  "cyrm_care"
)


# Run Spearman correlations

#Spearman correlation measures the strength and direction of a monotonic 
#relationship between two variables, using ranked data instead of raw values.

#less affected by outliers and doesn't need normal distributions to work

#measures monotonic not linear as the change isn't at a constant rate

results <- data.frame()

for(att in attention){

  for(res in resilience){

    # Keep only complete cases for this pair
    temp <- data[, c(att, res)]
    temp <- temp[complete.cases(temp), ]

    test <- cor.test(
      temp[[att]],
      temp[[res]],
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )

    results <- rbind(
      results,
      data.frame(
        Attention = att,
        Resilience = res,
        N = nrow(temp),
        Rho = unname(test$estimate),
        P = test$p.value
      )
    )

  }

}


# Multiple-comparison correction
#controls for false discovery rate

results$P_BH <- p.adjust(results$P, method = "BH")


# Round values


results$Rho <- round(results$Rho, 3)
results$P <- round(results$P, 4)
results$P_BH <- round(results$P_BH, 4)


# Add significance stars


results$Sig <- ifelse(results$P_BH < .001, "***",
               ifelse(results$P_BH < .01, "**",
               ifelse(results$P_BH < .05, "*", "")))


# Sort by adjusted p-value


results <- results[order(results$P_BH), ]


# View results


View(results)

print(results)


write.csv(
  results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/SART_Resilience_Correlations.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#visualize the correlations
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

heatmap_data <- results

heatmap_data$Attention <- factor(
  heatmap_data$Attention,
  levels = c(
    "meanrt",
    "stdrt",
    "err_com",
    "err_om",
    "imp_err3",
    "imp_err_total",
    "d_prime",
    "dsm_inatten",
    "bis_first",
    "bis_second"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "Mean RT",
    "RT Variability",
    "Commission Errors",
    "Omission Errors",
    "Impulsive Errors (3)",
    "Impulsive Errors (Total)",
    "d-prime",
    "DSM Inattention",
    "BIS First-order",
    "BIS Second-order"
  )
)

heatmap_data$Resilience <- factor(
  heatmap_data$Resilience,
  levels = c(
    "cdrisc",
    "cyrm_total",
    "cyrm_personal",
    "cyrm_care"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "CD-RISC",
    "CYRM Total",
    "CYRM Personal",
    "CYRM Caregiver"
  )
)

heatmap_data$Label <- sprintf("%.2f", heatmap_data$Rho)

heatmap_data$Label <- ifelse(
  heatmap_data$P_BH < .05,
  paste0(heatmap_data$Label, "*"),
  heatmap_data$Label
)

ggplot(heatmap_data,
       aes(x = Resilience,
           y = Attention,
           fill = Rho)) +

  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +

  geom_text(aes(label = Label),
            size = 4.5,
            fontface = "bold") +

  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#FA4616",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-0.5, 0.5),
    name = expression(r[s])
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Resilience Measure",
    y = "Attention Measure"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Correlation_Heatmap.png",
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 600
)
```
uses rho values and the astrik shows significant values (ofc postive and negative correlations)
